title: The Broken Horizon
premise: Ivo Pemberton, a debt-ridden storm chaser who measures life in miles, is hired by the creditors he fears to find the Meridian Star, an expedition vessel that went silent upriver carrying a salvaged memory-recording device worth a fortune. Racing a rival salvage fleet against six tides, Ivo discovers the expedition's sole survivor — a woman whose recorded memories have been overwritten with someone else's identity. As the river rises and his own buried past surfaces in the device's playback, Ivo must choose between selling the survivor to his creditors or destroying the machine that could rewrite anyone's self. He scuttles the wreck and the device beneath the final tide, pays his debts with truth instead of treasure, and drives inland for the first time in twenty years.
about_author: Theo Villalobos is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent a decade documenting salvage crews along forgotten waterways before turning to fiction. His work blends meteorological obsession with quiet meditations on what remains of a person when everything measurable is stripped away.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Chasing a supercell across the flats, Ivo calculates wind speed instead of his age, then returns to a dockside bar where creditors called 'the optimists' present him with a job: find the silent Meridian Star. Beat: dread disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. He meets Vess Corrigan, who smiles like weather about to turn, and signs a contract measured in tides rather than days. Flashback seeds: a fire, a name he no longer uses. Beat: signing away the last of his freedom.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Reviewing the expedition's final radio log, he hears a voice reading coordinates that don't exist, followed by thirty seconds of a lullaby no one on the crew list should know. Beat: the hook of the impossible.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. He buys passage on a rusting supply boat run by Captain Ondine Reyes, who knows the river better than any chart. First hints of the rival salvage fleet already two tides ahead. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Ondine. She reads Ivo's forged papers at a glance but says nothing, recognizing a man running from something upstream-shaped. They pass drowned villages where memory seems to pool like silt. Beat: wary mutual respect.

chapters.title: The Wreck Line
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Sonar finds debris fields too orderly to be accident — the Meridian Star was deliberately grounded. A rival skadow shadowing them fires a warning shot across the bow. Beat: the race turns hostile.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In a flooded cargo hold they find Sela March, alive, calm, and wrong — she introduces herself as Captain Aldous Wren, the expedition leader, a man she cannot possibly be. Beat: uncanny horror wrapped in relief.

chapters.title: Playback
chapters.summary: POV Sela. In fragments, we see her last true memories: a technician aboard the Star, watching the memory-device overwrite her during a failed experiment. Now she remembers Wren's life perfectly and her own not at all. Beat: grief without a self to grieve.

chapters.title: Tide Two
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The optimists radio demanding proof of salvage; Ivo lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Ondine catches the lie. Beat: corruption begins as convenience.

chapters.title: Wren's Log
chapters.summary: POV Sela-as-Wren. Using the captain's memories, she leads them through hidden compartments to the device itself, intact in its pressure case. She speaks of it with love, which terrifies Ivo. Beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Rival Fleet
chapters.summary: POV Ondine. The salvage fleet, led by ex-optimist enforcer Bram Kettle, boards at gunpoint but retreats when a flash storm hits. Ondine pilots them through white water no one should survive. Beat: adrenaline and deepening trust.

chapters.title: Miles Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Sheltering in a cliff cave, Ivo finally tells Sela about the fire twenty years ago — the one he caused, the name he buried. She listens with Wren's patience and asks who he'd be if he forgot. Beat: confession as turning point.

chapters.title: Tide Four
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Halfway point; the optimists threaten Ondine's family. Ivo realizes the device could erase his guilt entirely — a clean self, debt-free in every sense. Beat: the corrupt offer takes its true shape.

chapters.title: Sela's Lullaby
chapters.summary: POV Sela. A half-remembered melody surfaces that isn't Wren's — her mother's. She begins hunting her own erased life inside the device's backup archive, finding corrupted files and one intact: her real name. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Kettle's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Bram corners them at a trading post, offering to buy Sela and the device outright — enough to clear Ivo's debt twice over. Ivo stalls, and despises himself for considering it. Beat: the lowest moral ebb.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Ondine. Seasonal flood coming early; the wreck will be unreachable after tide five. Ondine declares her line: she carries people, not cargo, and won't ferry a woman sold. Beat: loyalty drawn as a hard border.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: POV Sela. Inside the device's full archive they discover Wren planned overwrites for the whole crew — a fleet of obedient selves for the optimists' buyers. Sela restores a sliver of herself and weeps with borrowed hands. Beat: stakes become civilization-scale.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The optimists arrive in person; Vess offers Ivo partnership if he delivers Sela, death if he doesn't. Ivo says yes — and means the opposite. Beat: the trap closes around the trapper.

chapters.title: Scuttle
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Climax part one: under cover of the rising tide, Ivo and Ondine breach the Meridian Star's hull with the device inside, while Sela floods the archive with noise — ten thousand false memories to poison any recovery. Beat: sacrifice in motion.

chapters.title: The Broken Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Sela. Climax part two: Vess holds a gun on Ivo as the wreck goes down; Sela, wearing Wren's authority like armor, convinces the optimists' own divers the device is cursed with unstable copies. Vess retreats ahead of the flood. Beat: identity wielded as a weapon.

chapters.title: Last Tide
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Aftermath: the river swallows the wreck whole. Ivo settles his debt by handing Vess the expedition's insurance ledger instead of treasure — evidence that ruins the optimists quietly. Sela chooses to rebuild herself from the recovered sliver. Beat: costly, earned release.

chapters.title: Inland
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Epilogue: Ondine drops him at a roadhead heading away from the coast. Sela, half-herself, rides along toward whatever name she'll grow into. Ivo measures the drive in hours for the first time in twenty years. Beat: quiet, open-ended renewal.
